record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Polyomino Tilings
record.original_question: For the problem of deciding whether a polyomino has a k-isohedral tiling, where k is the parameter, is the decision problem fixed-parameter tractable?

evidence.quote: A tiling T is k-isohedral provided that k is the smallest number of partitions in a partitioning of T such that for any two copies Ti, Tj in a common part, there is a symmetry of T mapping Ti to Tj.

When attempting to determine whether a polyomino has a k-isohedral tiling, one can use a similar approach as for isohedral tilings: derive a set of sufficient boundary criteria for k-isohedral tilings, then test the polyomino against the criteria set. However, the number of such criteria grow exponentially in k
Open Problem 7 (Asked in [27]) Is determining whether a polyomino has a k-isohedral tiling in FPT?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polyomino is a finite, edge-connected union of unit squares in the integer lattice. A tiling of the plane is a covering of the Euclidean plane by isometric copies of a prototile (in this case, a polyomino) such that the interiors of distinct copies are disjoint. Given a tiling T, two tiles are said to be in the same transitivity class if there is a symmetry of T (i.e., an isometry of the plane that maps T to itself) carrying one tile to the other. A tiling T is called k-isohedral if k is the smallest number of transitivity classes of T under its symmetry group; equivalently, k is the smallest integer such that the tiles of T can be partitioned into k parts where for any two tiles in the same part there is a symmetry of T mapping one to the other.

Consider the decision problem: given a polyomino P (encoded, e.g., by its boundary word or the list of its cells) and a positive integer k, determine whether there exists a k-isohedral tiling of the plane by isometric copies of P.

Question: Is this decision problem, parameterized by k, fixed-parameter tractable? That is, does there exist a computable function f and a constant c such that the problem can be solved in time f(k) · |P|^c, where |P| is the size of the input polyomino?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface any result establishing fixed-parameter tractability (or W[1]-hardness) for deciding the existence of a k-isohedral polyomino tiling parameterized by k. While the isohedral case (k=1) is known to be polynomial-time decidable, no general FPT algorithm or hardness result for the k-isohedral version appears in the available literature, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Isohedral Polyomino Tiling of the Plane
status_evidence.snippet: A polynomial time algorithm is given for deciding, for a given polyomino P, whether there exists an isohedral tiling of the Euclidean plane by isometric copies of P.
status_evidence.claim: The k=1 case is in P, but no extension to general k is given.

status_evidence.title: Polyform tiling (polyomino.org.uk)
status_evidence.snippet: Enumeration of k-isohedral tilings by polyforms aligned to underlying regular or Laves tilings.
status_evidence.claim: Existing work concerns enumeration in restricted settings, not parameterized complexity.
